THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A transfer to a sheet that already has someone with the same name or alias (ignoring case) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What happens on a merge** (in `PersonService.transfer`):
- The arriving claims are listed after the existing person's claims. They get the target sheet's next claim numbers and lose any figures a statement bound.
- The arriving name and aliases are added to the existing person's aliases.
- The other sheet writes `PERSON_TRANSFERRED … name=<name> from=<sheet id>`, then `PERSON_MERGED … from=<name> into=<name>`, then its usual rollup lines.
- The source sheet's records are unchanged.

**Choices the request didn't settle:**
- **Contact clash:** it no longer blocks a transfer that merges, because a merge drops the arriving person's contact.
- **Still refused:**
  - the arriving names match more than one person on the target sheet;
  - the matching person is retired (a merge refuses retired people too);
  - a name clashes with another sheet in the target sheet's tree.

**Stored-data change:** the test expects the merged person to show both `Addie` and `addie` as aliases. The old index refused two aliases that differ only in case. A new migration, `V73__person_alias_copy.sql`, adds an `alias_copy` counter to the index, so one person can hold both. Two different people still can't share an alias. `Person.addAlias` sets the counter.

The front end needed no change, since it already reloads the sheet after any transfer.
